1.text: How does tha city sit solitary, dat was full of people! how is she become as a widow! she dat was great among tha nations, N princess among tha provinces, how is she become tributary!
She weepeth sore in tha night, N her tears r on her cheeks: among all her lovers she has none 2 comfort her: all her friends have dealt treacherously wit her, dey r become her opps.
Judah is gone in2 captivity because of affliction, N because of great servitude: she lives among tha heathen, she finds no rest: all her persecutors overtook her between tha straits.
Tha ways of Zion do mourn, because none come 2 tha solemn feasts: all her gates r desolate: her priests sigh, her virgins r afflicted, N she is in bitterness.
Her adversaries r tha chief, her opps prosper; 4 tha LORD has afflicted her 4 tha crowd of her transgressions: her children r gone in2 captivity before tha opp.
N from tha daughter of Zion all her beauty is departed: her princes r become like harts dat find no pasture, N dey r gone without strength before tha pursuer.

Jerusalem remembered in tha days of her affliction N of her miseries all her pleasant things dat she had in tha days of old, when her people fell in2 tha hand of tha opp, N none did help her: tha adversaries saw her, N did mock at her sabbaths.
Jerusalem has grievously sinned; therefore she is removed: all dat honoured her despise her, because dey have seen her nakedness: yeah, she sigheth, N turns backward.
Her filthiness is in her skirts; she remembereth not her last end; therefore she came down wonderfully: she had no comforter. O LORD, look my affliction: 4 tha opp has magnified himself.
Tha adversary has spread out his hand upon all her pleasant things: 4 she has seen dat tha heathen entered in2 her sanctuary, whom u did command dat dey should not enter in2 ur congregation.
All her people sigh, dey seek bread; dey have given their pleasant things 4 food 2 relieve tha soul: see, O LORD, N consider; 4 I am become vile.
Is it nothing 2 u, all y’all dat pass by? look, N see if there be any sorrow like 2 my sorrow, which is done 2 me, wherewith tha LORD has afflicted me in tha day of his fierce anger.
From above has he sent fire in2 my bones, N it prevaileth against ’em: he has spread a net 4 my feet, he has turned me back: he has made me desolate N faint all tha day.

Tha yoke of my transgressions is bound by his hand: dey r wreathed, N come up upon my neck: he has made my strength 2 fall, tha Lord has delivered me in2 their hands, from whom I am not able 2 rise up.

Tha Lord has trodden under foot all my mighty men in tha midst of me: he has called an assembly against me 2 crush my young men: tha Lord has trodden tha virgin, tha daughter of Judah, as in a winepress.
4 dese things I weep; mine eye, mine eye runs down wit water, because tha comforter dat should relieve my soul is far from me: my children r desolate, because tha opp prevailed.
Zion spreads forth her hands, N there is none 2 comfort her: tha LORD has commanded concerning Jacob, dat his adversaries should be round about him: Jerusalem is as a menstruous woman among ’em.
Tha LORD is righteous; 4 I have rebelled against his commandment: hear, I pray u, all people, N look my sorrow: my virgins N my young men r gone in2 captivity.
I called 4 my lovers, but dey deceived me: my priests N mine elders gave up tha ghost in tha city, while dey sought their food 2 relieve their souls.
Look, O LORD; 4 I am in distress: my bowels r troubled; mine heart is turned within me; 4 I have grievously rebelled: abroad tha sword bereaveth, at home there is as death.
Dey have heard dat I sigh: there is none 2 comfort me: all mine opps have heard of my trouble; dey r glad dat u have done it: u will bring tha day dat u have called, N dey shall be like 2 me.
Let all their wickedness come before u; N do 2 ’em, as u have done 2 me 4 all my transgressions: 4 my sighs r many, N my heart is faint.

2.text: How has tha Lord covered tha daughter of Zion wit a cloud in his anger, N cast down from heaven 2 tha earth tha beauty of Israel, N remembered not his footstool in tha day of his anger!

Tha Lord has swallowed up all tha habitations of Jacob, N has not pitied: he has thrown down in his wrath tha strong holds of tha daughter of Judah; he has brought ’em down 2 tha ground: he has polluted tha kingdom N tha princes of it.
He has cut off in his fierce anger all tha horn of Israel: he has drawn back his right hand from before tha opp, N he burned against Jacob like a flaming fire, which devours round about.
He has bent his bow like an opp: he stood wit his right hand as an adversary, N killed all dat were pleasant 2 tha eye in tha tabernacle of tha daughter of Zion: he poured out his fury like fire.
Tha Lord was as an opp: he has swallowed up Israel, he has swallowed up all her palaces: he has destroyed his strong holds, N has increased in tha daughter of Judah mournin N lamentation.

N he has violently taken away his tabernacle, as if it were of a garden: he has destroyed his places of tha assembly: tha LORD has caused tha solemn feasts N sabbaths 2 be forgotten in Zion, N has despised in tha indignation of his anger tha king N tha priest.

Tha Lord has cast off his altar, he has abhorred his sanctuary, he has given up in2 tha hand of tha opp tha walls of her palaces; dey have made a noise in tha house of tha LORD, as in tha day of a solemn feast.

Tha LORD has purposed 2 destroy tha wall of tha daughter of Zion: he has stretched out a line, he has not withdrawn his hand from destroying: therefore he made tha rampart N tha wall 2 lament; dey languished together.
Her gates r sunk in2 tha ground; he has destroyed N broken her bars: her king N her princes r among tha Gentiles: tha law is no more; her prophets also find no vision from tha LORD.

Tha elders of tha daughter of Zion sit upon tha ground, N keep silence: dey have cast up dust upon their heads; dey have girded themselves wit sackcloth: tha virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads 2 tha ground.

My eyes do fail wit tears, my bowels r troubled, my liver is poured upon tha earth, 4 tha destruction of tha daughter of my people; because tha children N tha sucklings swoon in tha streets of tha city.
Dey say 2 their mothers, Where is corn N wine? when dey swooned as tha wounded in tha streets of tha city, when their soul was poured out in2 their mothers’ bosom.

What thing shall I take 2 witness 4 u? what thing shall I liken 2 u, O daughter of Jerusalem? what shall I equal 2 u, dat I may comfort u, O virgin daughter of Zion? 4 ur breach is great like tha sea: who can heal u?
Ur prophets have seen vain N foolish things 4 u: N dey have not discovered thine iniquity, 2 turn away ur captivity; but have seen 4 u false burdens N causes of banishment.
All dat pass by clap their hands at u; dey hiss N wag their head at tha daughter of Jerusalem, sayin, Is dis tha city dat men call tha perfection of beauty, tha joy of tha whole earth?
All thine opps have opened their mouth against u: dey hiss N gnash tha teeth: dey say, We have swallowed her up: certainly dis is tha day dat we looked 4; we have found, we have seen it.

Tha LORD has done dat which he had devised; he has fulfilled his word dat he had commanded in tha days of old: he has thrown down, N has not pitied: N he has caused thine opp 2 rejoice over u, he has set up tha horn of thine adversaries.
Their heart cried 2 tha Lord, O wall of tha daughter of Zion, let tears run down like a river day N night: give urself no rest; don’t let tha apple of thine eye cease.

Arise, cry out in tha night: in tha beginning of tha watches pour out thine heart like water before tha face of tha Lord: lift up ur hands toward him 4 tha life of ur young children, dat faint 4 hunger in tha top of every street.
Look, O LORD, N consider 2 whom u have done dis. Shall tha women eat their fruit, N children of a span long? shall tha priest N tha prophet be killed in tha sanctuary of tha Lord?
Tha young N tha old lie on tha ground in tha streets: my virgins N my young men r fallen by tha sword; u have killed ’em in tha day of thine anger; u have killed, N not pitied.
u have called as in a solemn day my terrors round about, so dat in tha day of tha LORD’s anger none escaped nor remained: dose dat I have swaddled N brought up has mine opp consumed.

3.text: I am tha man dat has seen affliction by tha rod of his wrath.
He has led me, N brought me in2 darkness, but not in2 light.
Surely against me is he turned; he turns his hand against me all tha day.
My flesh N my skin has he made old; he has broken my bones.
He has builded against me, N compassed me wit gall N travail.
He has set me in dark places, as dey dat be dead of old.
He has hedged me about, dat I cannot get out: he has made my chain heavy.
Also when I cry N shout, he shuts out my prayer.
He has inclosed my ways wit hewn stone, he has made my paths crooked.
He was 2 me as a bear lyin in wait, N as a lion in secret places.
He has turned aside my ways, N pulled me in pieces: he has made me desolate.
He has bent his bow, N set me as a mark 4 tha arrow.
He has caused tha arrows of his quiver 2 enter in2 my reins.
I was a derision 2 all my people; N their song all tha day.
He has filled me wit bitterness, he has made me drunken wit wormwood.
He has also broken my teeth wit gravel stones, he has covered me wit ashes.
N u have removed my soul far off from peace: I forgat prosperity.
N I said, My strength N my hope is perished from tha LORD:
Remembering mine affliction N my misery, tha wormwood N tha gall.
My soul has ’em still in remembrance, N is humbled in me.
Dis I recall 2 my mind, therefore have I hope.
It is of tha LORD’s mercies dat we r not consumed, because his compassions fail not.
Dey r new every morning: great is ur faithfulness.
Tha LORD is my portion, says my soul; therefore will I hope in him.
Tha LORD is good 2 ’em dat wait 4 him, 2 tha soul dat seeks him.
It is good dat a man should both hope N quietly wait 4 tha salvation of tha LORD.
It is good 4 a man dat he bear tha yoke in his youth.
He sits alone N keeps silence, because he has borne it upon him.
He puts his mouth in tha dust; if so be there may be hope.
He gives his cheek 2 him dat strikes him: he is filled full wit reproach.
4 tha Lord will not cast off 4 ever:
But though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according 2 tha crowd of his mercies.
4 he does not afflict willingly nor grieve tha children of men.
2 crush under his feet all tha prisoners of tha earth,
2 turn aside tha right of a man before tha face of tha most High,
2 subvert a man in his cause, tha Lord approveth not.
Who is he dat says, N it happens, when tha Lord commands it not?
Out of tha mouth of tha most High proceeds not evil N good?
So does a livin man complain, a man 4 tha punishment of his sins?
Let us search N try our ways, N turn again 2 tha LORD.
Let us lift up our heart wit our hands 2 God in tha heavenz.
We have transgressed N have rebelled: u have not pardoned.
u have covered wit anger, N persecuted us: u have killed, u have not pitied.
u have covered urself wit a cloud, dat our prayer should not pass through.
u have made us as tha offscouring N refuse in tha midst of tha people.
All our opps have opened their mouths against us.
Fear N a snare is come upon us, desolation N destruction.
Mine eye runs down wit rivers of water 4 tha destruction of tha daughter of my people.
Mine eye trickleth down, N ceases not, without any intermission,
Till tha LORD look down, N look from heaven.
Mine eye affecteth mine heart because of all tha daughters of my city.
Mine opps chased me sore, like a bird, without cause.
Dey have cut off my life in tha dungeon, N cast a stone upon me.
Waterz flowed over mine head; then I said, I am cut off.
I called upon ur name, O LORD, out of tha low dungeon.
u have heard my voice: hide not thine ear at my breathing, at my cry.
u drewest near in tha day dat I called upon u: u said, don’t fear.
O Lord, u have pleaded tha causes of my soul; u have redeemed my life.
O LORD, u have seen my wrong: judge u my cause.
u have seen all their vengeance N all their imaginations against me.
u have heard their reproach, O LORD, N all their imaginations against me;
Tha lips of dose dat rose up against me, N their device against me all tha day.
Look their sittin down, N their risin up; I am their musick.
Render 2 ’em a recompence, O LORD, according 2 tha work of their hands.
Give ’em sorrow of heart, ur curse 2 ’em.
Persecute N destroy ’em in anger from under tha heavenz of tha LORD.

4.text: How is tha gold become dim! how is tha most fine gold changed! tha stones of tha sanctuary r poured out in tha top of every street.
Tha precious sons of Zion, comparable 2 fine gold, how r dey esteemed as earthen pitchers, tha work of tha hands of tha potter!
Even tha sea monsters draw out tha breast, dey give suck 2 their young ones: tha daughter of my people is become cruel, like tha ostriches in tha wilderness.
Tha tongue of tha sucking child clings 2 tha roof of his mouth 4 thirst: tha young children ask bread, N no man breaks it 2 ’em.
Dey dat did feed delicately r desolate in tha streets: dey dat were brought up in scarlet embrace dunghills.
4 tha punishment of tha iniquity of tha daughter of my people is greater than tha punishment of tha sin of Sodom, dat was overthrown as in a moment, N no hands stayed on her.
Her Nazarites were purer than snow, dey were whiter than milk, dey were more ruddy in body than rubies, their polishing was of sapphire:
Their visage is blacker than a coal; dey r not known in tha streets: their skin clings 2 their bones; it is withered, it is become like a stick.
Dey dat be killed wit tha sword r better than dey dat be killed wit hunger: 4 dese pine away, stricken through 4 want of tha fruits of tha field.
Tha hands of tha pitiful women have sodden their own children: dey were their food in tha destruction of tha daughter of my people.
Tha LORD has accomplished his fury; he has poured out his fierce anger, N has kindled a fire in Zion, N it has devoured tha foundations of it.
Tha kings of tha earth, N all tha inhabitants of tha world, would not have believed dat tha adversary N tha opp should have entered in2 tha gates of Jerusalem.
4 tha sins of her prophets, N tha iniquities of her priests, dat have shed tha blood of tha just in tha midst of her,
Dey have wandered as blind men in tha streets, dey have polluted themselves wit blood, so dat men could not touch their garments.
Dey cried 2 ’em, Depart y’all; it is unclean; depart, depart, touch not: when dey fled away N wandered, dey said among tha heathen, dey shall no more stay there.
Tha anger of tha LORD has divided ’em; he will no more regard ’em: dey respected not tha persons of tha priests, dey favoured not tha elders.
As 4 us, our eyes as yet failed 4 our vain help: in our watchin we have watched 4 a nation dat could not save us.
Dey hunt our steps, dat we cannot go in our streets: our end is near, our days r fulfilled; 4 our end is come.
Our persecutors r swifter than tha eagles of tha heaven: dey pursued us upon tha mountains, dey laid wait 4 us in tha wilderness.
Tha breath of our nostrils, tha anointed of tha LORD, was taken in their pits, of whom we said, Under his shadow we shall live among tha heathen.
Rejoice N be glad, O daughter of Edom, dat dwell in tha land of Uz; tha cup also shall pass through 2 u: u will be drunken, N will make urself naked.
Tha punishment of thine iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Zion; he will no more carry u away in2 captivity: he will visit thine iniquity, O daughter of Edom; he will discover ur sins.

5.text: Remember, O LORD, what is come upon us: consider, N look our reproach.
Our inheritance is turned 2 strangers, our houses 2 aliens.
We r orphans N fatherless, our mothers r as widows.
We have drunken our water 4 money; our wood is sold 2 us.
Our necks r under persecution: we labour, N have no rest.
We have given tha hand 2 tha Egyptians, N 2 tha Assyrians, 2 be satisfied wit bread.
Our fathers have sinned, N r not; N we have borne their iniquities.
Servants have ruled over us: there is none dat does deliver us out of their hand.
We got our bread wit tha peril of our lives because of tha sword of tha wilderness.
Our skin was black like an oven because of tha terrible famine.
Dey ravished tha women in Zion, N tha maids in tha citiez of Judah.
Princes r hanged up by their hand: tha faces of elders were not honoured.
Dey took tha young men 2 grind, N tha children fell under tha wood.
Tha elders have ceased from tha gate, tha young men from their musick.
Tha joy of our heart is ceased; our dance is turned in2 mournin.
Tha crown is fallen from our head: woe 2 us, dat we have sinned!
4 dis our heart is faint; 4 dese things our eyes r dim.
Because of tha mountain of Zion, which is desolate, tha foxes walk upon it.
u, O LORD, remain 4 ever; ur throne from generation 2 generation.
So do u forget us 4 ever, N forsake us so long time?
Turn u us 2 u, O LORD, N we shall be turned; renew our days as of old.
But u have utterly rejected us; u r very angry against us.
